title: bank of england / financial stability / market structure | Speech Neutral | This time is different?
summary: Sarah Breeden, Deputy Governor for Financial Stability at the Bank of England, delivered a speech on April 17, 2026 assessing whether the financial system has learned from past crises and identifying current vulnerabilities. She acknowledges the system has proved resilient through six major shocks since 2020, but warns that risks have migrated from banks to market-based finance, private markets, and sovereign balance sheets. Breeden highlights three key structural vulnerabilities: the rapid growth of private markets to ~$18 trillion in global AuM, elevated sovereign debt near post-war highs, and complexity in interconnected financial ecosystems.
